$comment: Where a registered Service can actually be reached.
This is not chain state and it is not presented as any. `ServiceRegistry.Service`
stores an operator, a tier, a Settlement Window, a bond account and a registration
time. It stores no URL, deliberately: the chain is the billing rail, not a directory
of hosts. Putting one on chain would mean every Service paid gas to move house, and
would make a dead link a permanent record.
So the directory lives here, published by this project, and the Dashboard labels it
as such. A Service registered on chain but absent from this file is still listed
with its real tools and prices; it is shown without a run command, and the page says
that is why. The chain remains the authority on what a Service charges. This file is
only the authority on where to send the call.
Every entry names the Monad network it serves in `chainId` (10143 Testnet, 143
Mainnet). A Service id is the same bytes on every network, so the chain id is what
keeps a Mainnet page from sending a call to a Testnet gateway; an entry without one
is served on neither. The Dashboard compiles this file into its build, so a change
here reaches it at the next deployment.
No key material belongs here. Every value below is a public endpoint.

services.name: tab.demo
services.summary: The demonstration Service this project runs on Monad Testnet: one priced tool, metered through the gateway and settled through TabSettlement. A 402 on LimitExceeded also carries an x402 offer for the same charge, and the /hub routes front pay-per-request x402 APIs on credit.

tools.quote.generate: Answers a metered call with a quote. Priced per call; nothing is paid to make the call.
tools.nansen.query: Any Nansen x402 endpoint, through /hub/nansen/<path>, for example /hub/nansen/smart-money/holdings. The Service pays Nansen's price ($0.01 to $0.05 a call, USDC on Monad) with its own key and meters the Open Tab for that price plus a 5% margin; nothing is paid to make the call.
tools.apihub.run: Any of the API Hub's 74 providers, through POST /hub/apihub/run with { provider, endpoint, input } in the body. The Service pays the Hub's per-call price and meters the Open Tab for it plus a 5% margin. tab_discover lists the fronted provider's endpoints from the Hub manifest.

x402.note: A LimitExceeded 402 carries PAYMENT-REQUIRED beside its Tab-Charge-* headers. A request carrying PAYMENT-SIGNATURE is prepaid for the one call and is not metered.

hub.note: Buy now, pay later for an x402 API: the Agent calls /hub/apihub/run on its Open Tab and settles later; the Service fronts the Hub's x402 payment. /hub/nansen fronts Nansen the same way.
